target.title: feat(googlechat): support Application Default Credentials for outbound auth
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** the Google Chat channel only authenticates outbound calls with an explicit service-account credential (`serviceAccount` / `serviceAccountRef` / `serviceAccountFile`). There is no Application Default Credentials path, so a GCP-hosted gateway must keep a long-lived downloaded SA key on disk even though the runtime already has a usable identity (GCE metadata server / workload identity).
- **Change:** add an opt-in `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc: true`. When set and no explicit credential is configured, credential resolution returns a new `"adc"` source; the channel activates normally and the auth runtime constructs `GoogleAuth` without a key, falling back to the ambient ADC chain using the `chat.bot` scope.
- **Outcome:** GCP deployments can run Google Chat keyless — the attached service account / workload identity signs outbound requests, with no SA key in config or on disk. This mirrors how the Vertex model path already uses ADC.
- **Out of scope / unchanged:** the flag is opt-in and defaults off — existing `serviceAccount*` behavior is untouched, and an explicit credential always takes precedence. Inbound webhook auth (already keyless via `audience`/JWT) is not changed.
- **Reviewers, please focus on:** the new `"adc"` value in `accounts.ts` (`resolveCredentialsFromConfig`) and that it threads through the existing `credentialSource !== "none"` gates so the channel activates; the auth runtime already builds `GoogleAuth` with no credentials when none resolve, so no change was needed there.

## Linked context

Closes # _(none)_

Related # _(none found — searched issues for ADC/keyless Google Chat)_

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No — contributor-initiated. We run OpenClaw on GCP and want to eliminate Google Chat service-account key files.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Google Chat outbound auth required a downloaded SA key; with this patch it authenticates keyless via ADC.
- **Real environment tested:** OpenClaw `v2026.6.6` + this patch, built into the Docker image and deployed on a GCE VM (arm64). Google Chat app configured (Workspace add-on, app-url audience). The VM's attached service account is the Chat app's posting identity and carries the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chat.bot` access scope. No service-account key exists in the config or on the VM disk.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** set `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc: true` with **no** `serviceAccountRef`/`serviceAccountFile` (and removed the on-disk key those previously pointed at), restarted the gateway, then sent the bot a direct message and confirmed the reply.
- **Evidence after fix:** Copied live output / redacted runtime logs and a reply screenshot from a real GCE deployment (identifiers — space id, message/run/session ids, add-on principal, webhook path key — redacted). Three artifacts:

  **(1) Keyless config in effect** — the live `channels.googlechat` block: ADC on, no credential of any kind configured:
  ```json
  "googlechat": {
    "serviceAccountAdc": true,
    "audienceType": "app-url",
    "audience": "https://<redacted-host>/<redacted-path-key>/googlechat",
    "webhookPath": "/<redacted-path-key>/googlechat"
  }
  ```

  **(2) Runtime round-trip log** — an inbound DM driven all the way to a delivered reply on `channel=googlechat`, with no credential/key anywhere in the pipeline (note the only outbound HTTP the transport logs is the model call to Anthropic; the Chat send is the dispatch that completes at the end):
  ```
  [diagnostic] message received: channel=googlechat chatId=googlechat:spaces/<redacted> messageId=<redacted> sessionKey=agent:main:main source=dispatchInboundMessage
  [agent/embedded] embedded run start: runId=<redacted> provider=anthropic model=claude-opus-4-7 messageChannel=googlechat
  [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-opus-4-7 status=200
  [googlechat] embedded run agent end: runId=<redacted> isError=false
  [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=googlechat sessionKey=agent:main:main source=replyResolver outcome=completed duration=5675ms
  [diagnostic] message processed: channel=googlechat chatId=googlechat:spaces/<redacted> outcome=completed duration=5758ms
  ```

  **(3) Reply artifact** — the bot's reply rendered in Google Chat (keyless; no SA key configured):

  ![Keyless Google Chat reply — the bot ("Cora") replies to a DM with serviceAccountAdc enabled and no service-account key configured](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc604362-c55e-41bc-8bee-a169d01b1cf1)

  For completeness, the gateway boot with `serviceAccountAdc: true` and no Chat credential — the channel loads and mounts its webhook with no credential error:
  ```
  [googlechat] [default] starting Google Chat webhook
  [gateway] ready
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the googlechat channel activates on `credentialSource: "adc"` and mounts its webhook; an inbound DM is processed to `outcome=completed` and the bot replies (screenshot). Because **no credential of any kind is configured and no key file is on disk**, the outbound post to `chat.googleapis.com` can only have authenticated via the ambient ADC identity — the VM's attached service account (`chat.bot` scope) through the GCE metadata server. A misconfigured/absent ADC identity would fail the outbound send; the delivered reply confirms the ADC path worked.
- **What was not tested:** the `project-number` audience type (we use `app-url`); non-GCE ADC sources such as `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (only the GCE metadata path was exercised); multi-account `channels.googlechat.accounts.*` setups (see review note below).
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** private deployment; identifiers redacted. I did not capture a discrete metadata-server token-fetch log line: the ADC access token is cached in-process after first acquisition, so a subsequent DM within the token lifetime triggers no fresh metadata call to log. The token-source claim therefore rests on (a) no credential being configured anywhere and (b) the outbound reply succeeding — which together are only possible via the ambient ADC identity.
- **Before evidence (optional):** before the patch, the same config failed at startup — `channels.googlechat: invalid config: must not have additional properties: "serviceAccountAdc"` (unknown key), and with no credential at all the channel stayed `credentialSource: "none"` and never mounted its webhook.

## Tests and validation

Commands run (rebased onto current `main`, regenerated artifacts, re-run):
- `pnpm test:extension googlechat` — **pass**, including the added `resolveGoogleChatAccount` cases (`serviceAccountAdc` → `source: "adc"`; explicit credential still wins) and the schema-accept case.
- `pnpm config:channels:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm config:schema:check` — green after regenerating `bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` and the config-doc baseline (`config:channels:gen` / `config:docs:gen`).

Regression coverage added: `extensions/googlechat/src/setup.test.ts` (resolver: adc source + explicit-wins) and `extensions/googlechat/src/config-schema.test.ts` (schema accepts `serviceAccountAdc`).

What failed before this fix: unknown-key config rejection, and a credential-less channel never activating (`credentialSource: "none"`).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? **No** — opt-in, default off.
- Config/env/migration change? **Yes** — new optional config key `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc`.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec change? **Yes** — adds an ADC auth path for Chat outbound and removes the need to store a service-account key file.
- Highest-risk area: an operator enabling `serviceAccountAdc` where ADC is unavailable/unauthorized would see outbound auth fail at runtime.
- Mitigation: strictly opt-in; an explicit credential always takes precedence; the channel only uses ADC when the operator asks for it and supplies no key. Docs note the required `chat.bot` scope.

## Current review state

- Next action: maintainer review + CI authorization (heavy CI lanes are gated behind first-time-contributor workflow-actor approval).
- Rebased onto current `main`; generated artifacts (`bundled-channel-config-metadata`, config-doc baseline) regenerated; real-behavior proof above (round-trip runtime log + reply screenshot).
- **Addressed since the ClawSweeper review — multi-account credential surfaces:** `serviceAccountAdc` is now treated as credential-owned config everywhere the older key fields are — registered as an implicit-default-account key, excluded from `accounts.default` shared defaults (no cross-account ambient-ADC inheritance), and cleared alongside the key fields on default-account deletion. Added multi-account regression tests in `extensions/googlechat/src/accounts.test.ts`.
- **Open for maintainer direction — Compute metadata-server boundary:** ADC resolves tokens via `google-auth-library`/`gcp-metadata`'s standard metadata path, outside any Chat-specific fetch guard. This is opt-in (`serviceAccountAdc` defaults off) and our own deployment is single-account on GCE, so ADC-via-metadata is the intended path for us — flagging for an explicit accept-or-guard decision, and happy to add a guard instead if preferred.
